hypothesis: Bounded canonical single-block map/reduce loops can split before whole-loop canVectorize or VPlan construction. Independent integer-add and ordinary float/double-add reductions consume original contributions from private bounded scratch. A safe scalar helper without a vector mapping can keep the producer scalar while normal LV vectorizes the consumer. Arithmetic-only producers and one or multiple reductions use the same path without pressure, chain-depth, reduction-count or original-vectorizability prerequisites. This revision repairs validation, including repeated inner producer/consumer stages inside an existing outer loop; it adds no new semantic transformation or profitability gate.
semantics: Scalar-fission legality and emission remain unchanged: exact bounded participating iterations, initial values, operand order, wrap/FP flags, guards and final-reduction live-outs are retained; private scratch requires no alias assumptions. Calls still require explicit memory(none), nounwind, willreturn and speculatable contracts, and strict/constrained FP and unsupported dependences remain rejected. Default RVV EVL checks now tie get.vector.length, VP loads and ordered VP FP reductions to the same active count, with integer inactive-lane merges, EVL-based progress and termination. Explicit dont-fold-tail checks retain ordinary vector loads/reductions and scalar remainders. Both variants receive RVV machine-verification RUNs. The executable checker extracts whole multiline definitions with explicit missing/duplicate failures, checks each exact consumer separately from its producer and other functions, and inserts host-only probes after that consumer header's PHIs. Both settings of the separate fission FP option retain exact scalar-IR comparisons for integer and ordered float/double, zero/one/odd/tail/max counts, rejected guards, input/output aliasing and narrow IVs. Host execution uses only the labeled dont-fold-tail, epilogue-vectorization-disabled variant; specialization fails on EVL/VP instead of silently retaining unsupported vector-length or mask semantics. A supported fixed VF=4 narrow-IV consumer is also instrumented and required to execute. The nested fixture carries integer/double inner results to the next outer iteration, exports every row, overwrites the same entry scratch on each row, and compares future-row input/output aliasing. Null pointers exercise rejected outer/inner guards; repeated vector-consumer visits are counted. Loop, dominator and scalar-evolution verification remain, including repeated vectorizer invocation. Legacy VPlan and rejection coverage are retained. No compiler, build, test runner or execution checker was invoked by this worker.
costs: One static entry alloca per distinct contribution, shared by SSA identity. An element size S and proven capacity M use M*S storage plus ABI padding and 2*N*S logical scratch traffic per invocation. Existing fixtures: helper 260 bytes/8*N traffic; arithmetic i64 520 bytes/16*N; mixed four reductions and three slots 1044 bytes including 4 padding bytes/32*N; narrow 800 bytes/1600 traffic at N=200; single iteration 4 bytes/8 traffic. New nested fixture: 65 i32 and 65 double elements, 784 layout bytes including 4 padding bytes, reused every row, with 24*Rows*N traffic bytes. Capacity does not multiply by the row count. Input reads/helper calls occur once per participating iteration without duplication, rereads or recomputation; outer alias stores precede the next row's producer. Loop control repeats, and ordinary LV supplies independent stage minimum-trip/tail checks. Original guards remain with no added alias/SCEV guards or unbounded storage. Compiler analysis remains linear instruction/use checks plus existing SCEV bounds, LI updates, enclosing-nest SE invalidation, dominator recalculation and loop-access cache clearing. This revision adds checker/test complexity: labeled tail variants, exact-function parsing and consumer-scoped validation, a small nested fixture and fixed narrow-IV execution. Host-only probe calls perturb code and are excluded from RVV codegen inputs; no performance inference is made.
limitations: All new/changed checks await independent harness compilation and validation; no passing result or new corpus coverage is claimed. Default EVL has IR assertions and RVV codegen/machine verification only, not host execution. Host fixed-vscale scalar-tail and fixed-VF execution are separately labeled and are neither RVV target execution nor speedup measurements. The specializer deliberately has no VP/EVL semantics implementation. General CFG/conditional participation, early exits, unsupported recurrences/live-outs, writes inside candidate loops, volatile/atomic accesses, read-only-memory or unsafe calls and strict/constrained FP remain unsupported. The nested fixture covers a bounded outer loop with a canonical single-block inner reduction, not arbitrary loop nests. Multiline parsing is scoped to these fixtures' unquoted function names and LLVM's printed closing-brace format. No new profitability model or target-runtime measurements are included.
evidence: Read BENCHMARKS_ANALYSIS.md, frozen SWIFT t000002 and LibSVM t000016 sources/check.json evidence, immutable t000002.patch, and the t000002 revision review/lit failure log. That log records successful compilation followed by FileCheck failures on default VP loads and ordered VP fadd; mandatory execution and primary-corpus evidence were absent. Frozen examples motivate early splitting but do not establish that the initial call/CFG contracts apply to those benchmark loops. All 117 original evaluation inputs remain unchanged.
test_expectations: Prior ordinary-load/vector.reduce.fadd/scalar-tail expectations were inaccurate for default RVV LV, which selects EVL tail folding. They are replaced by explicit EVL/VP participation, progress, ordered-FP and shared-contribution assertions; ordinary operations and scalar remainders remain in a separate explicit dont-fold-tail RUN. Selected/Rejected source remarks, independent stage VF/scratch evidence, disabled/limit/overflow/fixed-width checks, live-outs, double invocation, every rejection case and legacy VPlan-path fixtures remain. The fixed-width RUN explicitly uses dont-fold-tail too. Forced widths and tail options make validation deterministic; they are not legality prerequisites and do not change benchmark policies. The Python regression rejects missing/duplicate functions, a producer reduction used as consumer evidence, and unsupported EVL/VP specialization.

harness_required: All existing fission lit tests and the explicit lit paths in tests
llvm/utils/check-reduction-fission.py with default vscales 1,2,4,8,32, both FP-option settings, nested and fixed-narrow cases
All 117 unchanged original benchmarks under strict and FP-reordered primary policies
validation_requested.expected_outcomes: Default EVL assertions match observed VP emission; supported scalar-tail consumers execute with exact ordered results, including repeated nested scratch reuse and real outer alias dependence. Actual results must be supplied by the harness.
